summary: Siskiyou forest lookout on Sanger Peak from 1916; a house built 1926 was replaced in 1957; only remains of the lookout are on the summit today.

facts.design: Standard U.S. Forest Service lookout house, about 14 feet square
facts.status_note: Only the remains of the lookout are on the summit, per the Forest Service.

access.note: Forest Road 4803 from Highway 199 (by Waldo Road or Knopki Creek Road), then a 0.6-mile Forest Service trail to the summit.

visit.trail_note: 0.6-mile trail, moderate to strenuous, steep and rocky in places.

events.note: Worth Hamilton joined the Forest Service to act as lookout (July 1916 item)
Two women installed at the station near Takilma
Ready-cut cabin packed in from Page Creek and built on the peak; house complete by September 1926
Aircraft Warning Service station placed on inactive status but retained on inventory; service added sleeping quarters
New 15 by 15 ft flat-top lookout tower set to replace the old house; photo page says rebuilt in 1957
Dennis Bottel employed as lookout in summer 1961
Dennis Bottel due to spend the 1962 summer as lookout

corrections.why: A 1957 item on the page calls the replacement a lookout tower, and a 1952 survey note puts the house about 25 feet high. The FFLA list types the site Ground. Not checked on the ground; for a human to confirm.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A Peakbagging photo page places the lookout in Six Rivers National Forest; the Forest Service trail page names the Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest, and the Weebly page names the Siskiyou National Forest. The Forest Service's current name is used.

sources.title: Sanger Peak Lookout Trail #1270
sources.publisher: Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest, USDA Forest Service

notes_for_editor: Remains on the summit are confirmed by two sources (a 2005 photo page and the Forest Service); neither says which lookout generation they are. A search snippet for a 360Cities panorama describes foundations of the 1926 and 1957 towers, but that page returned 403 and is not cited. The 1939 forest history and the 1919 diary are quoted through the Weebly page, not read directly. Agency and kind are the two points for a human to check; the kind correction is unverified.
